name: Dana Patel

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What happens in a normal day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I handle calls and chats about missed grocery orders. I have been here nine years and can solve the usual substitutions, though the complicated refund cases still go to the strongest agents. I finished secondary school, work at about the middle of the team, and my pay is at the lower end. I use the approved AI search every day, then check the actual order receipt before offering a credit.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is waiting after your shift?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58 and my husband Vikram sells flowers at a market, where earnings depend on the week. Our grown daughter lives separately. We rent a flat and have just over two weeks of expenses saved. There are few other contact centres nearby. I used to work hotel breakfasts, and I cannot yet say what income would let me stop doing full weeks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team the search tool helps find an old order, but somebody still has to look at the receipt. A missing loaf is one thing; a charge for a whole order that never arrived is another.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my calls to continue. Vikram’s market income rises and falls, so our two-week reserve still feels small next to rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep handling grocery complaints and checking AI suggestions against the order receipt. In the first year we will take a flask of tea to work instead of buying drinks at the station and put the saved amount beside rent each week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel settled about the queue and tense about money. The tool may be quick, but the landlord wants a real payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the tool mix up?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It found a similar order from the same customer but the wrong day. I checked the receipt before issuing a credit for someone else’s groceries.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your daughter help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: She has her own flat and bills. We enjoy dinner together, but our rent plan is ours.

say: I would use **AI search** with original receipt checks.
I would separate a **missing item** from a whole lost order.
think: I expect my **grocery calls** to continue.
I know Vikram’s **variable market income** keeps rent tight even while my own call hours hold.
do: Keep checking **grocery receipts** before issuing credits.
Bring a **tea flask** and save former station-drink spending for rent.
S0.quote: The tool may be quick, but the landlord wants a real payment.
fieldNote: Her **nine years** make her experienced on common grocery problems, while complex refunds still go to stronger agents.
Daily AI search still needs **receipt dates**.
The **drink cut** creates repeatable rent savings.

steps.text: Keep checking grocery-order receipts before approving AI-suggested credits
Bring tea flask instead of buying station drinks
Put former station-drink spending beside weekly rent money

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say automated replies should be measured by the orders customers call about twice. Fast closures are not much help if a family still has no dinner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can learn a better checking screen, but easy missing-item chats might go before I have a different paid task. Our rent has little patience for a lost day.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I will learn the new AI exception view on twenty closed substitutions during paid shifts and count wrong credits. I will take the list to my manager and ask what paid complaint hours remain. If my rota shrinks in the first year, I will apply for posted paid hotel breakfast shifts only when the full weekly pay covers rent and the early journey is possible from our flat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing hours, although testing gives me a little control. I like a new tool when it catches the wrong bag, not when it replaces the wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a hotel remember you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know breakfast service, but the staff have changed since I left. I need a posted paid shift; a familiar dining room is not a vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Vikram check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: He opens his flower stall early, so I would check the first bus before agreeing to a breakfast start. A high hourly rate is useless if I cannot reach the hotel.

say: I would count **repeat grocery calls** after automated closures, including families still waiting for an order.
I would show **wrong credits** to my manager.
think: I can learn **AI exceptions** but still lose shifts.
Our **thin rent reserve** cannot absorb a lost day easily.
do: Learn **AI exception view** on twenty closed substitutions during paid shifts.
Ask manager about **remaining paid complaint hours** with an error list.
Seek **posted paid breakfast shifts** after cuts only with rent-covering weekly pay and a reachable early bus.
S1.quote: I need a posted paid shift; a familiar dining room is not a vacancy.
fieldNote: The **new AI view** is learning beyond daily search.
Her manager approach is **individual**, not group bargaining.
A **first bus** is a practical gate for hotel work.

steps.text: Learn new AI exception view on twenty closed substitutions during paid shifts
Show manager wrong-credit list and ask about remaining paid complaint hours
Apply after cuts for posted breakfast work with rent-covering weekly pay and reachable early bus

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the desk full thinking AI by 2028 could settle most grocery complaints from the receipt alone. Robots around 2031 come later and do not keep our headsets paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my ordinary call hours could disappear. Two weeks saved and a changing flower-market wage cannot carry rent through a long search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will ask for a written rota-change date and postpone buying a new kitchen shelf while the old one stays secure. If the calls end in the first year after 2028, I will apply for advertised paid hotel breakfast work; I will take it only if the full weekly wages cover rent and travel and the first bus gets me there.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed about losing a regular week. I can make breakfast for a crowd, but I cannot make a hotel open a vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would robots reach that work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They could reach serving and cleaning around 2031. I would treat a hotel shift as paid work for now, not proof it stays forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the shelf is unsafe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If it tilts, Vikram and I will secure it before we keep using it. We will buy another if we cannot make this one safe.

say: I would warn **2028 AGI** threatens grocery calls before I can find another regular week.
I would separate **2031 robots** from desk risk.
think: I know two weeks saved and **market wages** cannot carry rent through a long hotel search.
do: Request **written rota date** and delay shelf purchase only while secure; repair any tilt before replacing.
Apply after cuts for **advertised paid breakfast**; take it only if full weekly wages cover rent, travel and a reachable first bus.
S2.quote: I can make breakfast for a crowd, but I cannot make a hotel open a vacancy.
fieldNote: The **shelf delay** ends if it cannot be made safe.
Breakfast work is **temporary paid work**, not permanent shelter.
Her old hotel experience needs a **real vacancy**.

steps.text: Delay shelf purchase while secure; fix any tilt and replace only if repair cannot make safe
Apply for advertised paid hotel breakfast; take only with rent/travel-covering full-week wages and reachable first bus

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years gives us time to check real paid shifts before calls change. General AI reaches grocery complaints in 2031; hands-on robots follow around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might keep handling complicated orders while I look at hotel work. I do not know whether breakfast service will have paid hours then, so I will not count it yet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep my calls and ask two hotels for their posted breakfast rotas. If a paid opening appears with full weekly pay covering rent and travel and an early bus I can catch, I will ask a cook to show me the current service routine during a paid shift. In the first year after 2031 I will move only when the paid hours actually exist.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but a few years lets me see the kitchen on a real workday. I cannot plan rent from a hotel menu.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not need a new certificate to arrange a breakfast table. I do need the cook to show me current food rules during paid work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Vikram change his stall hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, the early market is his main income. I would fit a hotel shift around that rather than assume his wage can bend around mine.

say: I would check **posted breakfast hours** and the actual full week of pay before moving.
I would separate **2031 calls** from later robots.
think: I may keep **complicated orders** on my current paid shift while the hotel route is checked.
I cannot budget an **unposted hotel shift**.
do: Learn **current food rules** during paid coaching only for posted hotel work with full-week rent-and-travel-covering pay and reachable bus.
Move after 2031 only with **actual paid hours** fitting Vikram’s stall schedule.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to inspect a real kitchen.
S3.quote: I cannot plan rent from a hotel menu.
fieldNote: Paid coaching covers **current food rules**, not a bought course.
The **early bus** and Vikram’s stall time limit a move.
No hotel menu is a substitute for **paid hours**.

steps.text: Keep taking paid grocery complaint calls while shifts remain
Ask two hotels for posted paid breakfast rotas with rent-and-travel-covering full-week wages and early bus
Learn current food rules from cook during paid shift only if qualifying role opens
Move after 2031 only for real paid hours fitting Vikram’s market schedule

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell people a decade gives us time to earn and compare real weekly pay. General AI reaches calls in 2036; hands-on robots follow around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 68 I may want fewer hours, but we have not agreed what income replaces my wage. Two weeks saved makes this month’s rent real even in a slow picture.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will keep taking grocery calls and put a small fixed amount from each pay into a rent reserve. Each year I will check posted centre and hotel rotas. In the first year after 2036, if call hours fall, I will accept another paid shift only if the full week covers rent and travel and the start fits Vikram’s market day.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about our money now, though I have time to compare later work. Ten years is no answer to a rent bill due next week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you stop full-time work sooner?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if we can name the wages that pay the flat. I am not adding a pension amount we have not confirmed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your daughter contribute?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: She has her own flat to support. We can share supper without asking her to fund our rent.

say: I would compare **full weekly wages** over the decade, including the journey to an early hotel shift.
I would separate **2036 calls** from later robots.
think: I cannot name **income at 68** replacing wages.
I know two weeks saved leaves **rent urgent** today despite a longer preparation window.
do: Keep **grocery calls** and save a fixed pay amount.
Check **posted rotas** at contact centres and hotels each year.
Accept after cuts only **paid weekly work** covering rent and travel with Vikram-compatible start times.
feel: **Anxious** about current rent despite extra time.
S4.quote: Ten years is no answer to a rent bill due next week.
fieldNote: Her **rent reserve** grows from actual pay.
She assumes **no pension** or daughter support.
The hotel start must fit **Vikram’s market** hours.
A **full week** matters more than an attractive hourly hotel rate.

steps.text: Keep taking paid grocery complaint calls
Save fixed amount from each pay into rent reserve
Accept paid work after cuts only with weekly rent-and-travel-covering wages and compatible market hours
Compare posted centre and hotel rotas yearly

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. A regular call week could vanish before a hotel pays me for a breakfast shift. A written date and an advertised paid job with enough weekly money for rent and travel would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who checks the order receipt when a machine says a bag arrived. A customer cannot cook a neat reply. Someone must check the food that reached the door.

headlineQuote: A customer cannot cook a neat reply.
portrait: Dana is a **58-year-old experienced agent** with secondary schooling, average skill and lower pay.
She uses **AI daily** but checks receipts; Vikram’s flower-market earnings vary.
With **two weeks saved** and few nearby centres, rent remains urgent across all five pictures.
She considers **posted hotel breakfast work** only when weekly pay and the first bus make it real.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase her regular grocery calls before paid hotel work opens.
whatWouldHelp: A **written date** and advertised paid work with rent-and-travel-covering weekly wages would help.
